items.stem: How is frequency density calculated?
items.answer: frequency ÷ class width
items.markingKey: Frequency density = frequency / class width.

items.stem: Explain why frequency density, not frequency, is used for the heights of bars when class widths are unequal.
items.answer: A wider class would look too important if height showed frequency; using frequency density makes the area of each bar proportional to its frequency.
items.markingKey: B1 wider classes exaggerated; B1 area ∝ frequency [2]

items.stem: Explain how to find the frequency of a class from a histogram.
items.answer: Multiply the frequency density (bar height) by the class width (bar width), i.e. find the area of the bar.
items.markingKey: B1 height × width; B1 area = frequency [2]

items.stem: The table shows the waiting time at a clinic. 0 < w ≤ 5: 18; 5 < w ≤ 10: 25; 10 < w ≤ 20: 8; 20 < w ≤ 40: 20; 40 < w ≤ 60: 88 (w in minutes). Calculate the frequency density for the class 40 < w ≤ 60.

The table shows the mass of apples. 100 < m ≤ 120: 64; 120 < m ≤ 140: 24; 140 < m ≤ 150: 10; 150 < m ≤ 160: 16; 160 < m ≤ 180: 100; 180 < m ≤ 220: 16 (m in g). Calculate the frequency density of each class, ready to draw a histogram.
items.markingKey: M1 frequency ÷ class width for each; A2 all correct (A1 for at least three correct).

items.stem: A class 0 < x ≤ 50 has a frequency of 12. What is the frequency density?
Explain why the modal class of data with unequal widths is the class with the highest frequency density, not the highest frequency.
items.answer: The modal class is where the data are most concentrated per unit of the variable, which is shown by the tallest bar (largest frequency density).
items.markingKey: B1 concentration per unit width; B1 tallest bar [2]

items.stem: Grace draws a histogram of the height of seedlings. For the class 50 < h ≤ 70, which has frequency 64, Grace draws a bar of height 64. Explain the error and give the correct height.
items.answer: The class width is 20, so the bar height must be the frequency density 64 ÷ 20 = 3.2.
items.markingKey: B1 must use frequency density; B1 3.2 [2]

items.stem: Mei draws a histogram of the daily rainfall. For the class 90 < r ≤ 110, which has frequency 48, Mei draws a bar of height 48. Explain the error and give the correct height.

items.markingKey: B1 must use frequency density; B1 2.4 [2]

items.stem: Samuel draws a histogram of the distance thrown in a javelin competition. For the class 80 < d ≤ 100, which has frequency 40, Samuel draws a bar of height 40. Explain the error and give the correct height.

items.stem: When drawing a cumulative frequency curve from grouped data, each point is plotted at
items.answer: the upper class boundary
items.markingKey: Cumulative frequency counts values up to the end of each class.

items.stem: Explain why cumulative frequencies are plotted at upper class boundaries and not at midpoints.
items.answer: The cumulative frequency is the number of values less than or equal to the end of the class; only at the upper boundary are all those values included.
items.markingKey: B1 counts values up to end of class; B1 upper boundary [2]

items.stem: Explain why a cumulative frequency curve can never go down.
items.answer: Each new class adds a frequency of zero or more to the running total, so the total never decreases.
items.markingKey: B1 adding non-negative frequencies; B1 never decreases [2]

items.stem: The last value in a cumulative frequency table is equal to
items.answer: the total frequency
items.markingKey: It counts all the values.

items.stem: Describe how to use a cumulative frequency curve to find how many values are greater than a given value.
items.answer: Read the cumulative frequency at that value and subtract it from the total frequency.
items.markingKey: B1 read CF; B1 subtract from total [2]

items.stem: Explain why the interquartile range is often a better measure of spread than the range.
items.answer: The range depends only on the two extreme values, which may be outliers; the IQR covers the middle 50% so is not affected by extremes.
items.markingKey: B1 range uses extremes; B1 IQR middle 50% [2]

items.stem: Explain what it means if the 10th percentile of journey times is 12 minutes.
items.answer: 10% of the journeys took 12 minutes or less (and 90% took longer).
items.markingKey: B1 10% at or below; B1 in context [2]

items.stem: A cumulative frequency curve is drawn for 485 measurements of the distance thrown in a javelin competition in Karachi (d in m). How is the interquartile range calculated?
items.answer: Upper quartile − lower quartile
items.markingKey: IQR = Q₃ − Q₁, the range of the middle 50%.

items.stem: Describe how to find the lower quartile from a cumulative frequency curve for 120 values.
items.answer: Find 30 (one quarter of 120) on the cumulative frequency axis, go across to the curve and down to read the value.
items.markingKey: B1 n/4 = 30; B1 read across and down [2]

items.stem: From a cumulative frequency curve, the lowest value is 20, the lower quartile is 31, the upper quartile is 69 and the highest value is 94. Mei says the interquartile range is 94 − 20 = 74. Explain the error and find the correct interquartile range.
items.answer: Mei has found the range. IQR = upper quartile − lower quartile = 69 − 31 = 38.
items.markingKey: B1 range vs IQR; B1 38 [2]

items.stem: From a cumulative frequency curve, the lowest value is 35, the lower quartile is 40, the upper quartile is 49 and the highest value is 84. Nadia says the interquartile range is 84 − 35 = 49. Explain the error and find the correct interquartile range.

(b) Estimate the 90th percentile.
When comparing two distributions, which pair of statistics is most useful?
options: The modal class and total frequency
An average and a measure of spread
The smallest and largest values only
items.answer: An average and a measure of spread
items.markingKey: For example the median and the interquartile range.

items.stem: Group A has IQR 8 and group B has IQR 15. Which statement is correct?
options: Group A has a higher median
items.answer: Group A is more consistent
items.markingKey: A smaller IQR means the middle 50% of values are closer together.

items.stem: Explain why a comparison of two distributions should refer to the context.
items.answer: Statements such as "the median is higher" only become meaningful when they say what this means, for example that Class A students generally scored higher marks.
items.markingKey: B1 statistics alone not enough; B1 interpret in context [2]

items.stem: On two cumulative frequency curves drawn on the same axes for the same number of items, the curve further to the right shows

items.stem: Explain why a histogram and a cumulative frequency curve might both be useful when comparing two distributions.
items.answer: A histogram shows the shape and modal class; a cumulative frequency curve allows the median and quartiles to be estimated and compared.

items.stem: Give a reason for each answer. (a) Explain why the interquartile range is often a better measure of spread than the range. (b) Describe how to find the lower quartile from a cumulative frequency curve for 120 values.
items.answer: (a) The range depends only on the two extreme values, which may be outliers; the IQR covers the middle 50% so is not affected by extremes. (b) Find 30 (one quarter of 120) on the cumulative frequency axis, go across to the curve and down to read the value.
items.markingKey: (a) B1 range uses extremes; B1 IQR middle 50% [2] (b) B1 n/4 = 30; B1 read across and down [2]

items.stem: A cumulative frequency curve is drawn for 131 measurements of the mass of parcels at a depot in Cairo (m in kg). It passes through (0, 0) and the points m ≤ 15: 9; m ≤ 20: 27; m ≤ 30: 67; m ≤ 40: 83; m ≤ 60: 131. Assume it is straight between these points. (a) Estimate the median. (b) Estimate the 10th percentile. (c) Explain what the interquartile range tells you about the data.
items.answer: (a) 29.6 kg (b) 16.1 kg (c) The middle 50% of the mass values lie within a range of about 24.9 kg.

items.stem: The heights of sunflowers of Garden X have median 117 cm and interquartile range 6 cm. The heights of sunflowers of Garden Y have median 147 cm and interquartile range 7 cm. Make two comparisons between the distributions.
items.answer: The median for Garden Y is higher, so Garden Y generally had taller sunflowers. The IQR for Garden X is smaller, so the heights of sunflowers for Garden X are more consistent (less spread).
items.markingKey: B1 comparison of medians in context; B1 comparison of IQRs in context [2]

items.stem: What is plotted on the vertical axis of a histogram with unequal class widths?
items.answer: Frequency density
items.markingKey: Using frequency density makes the areas proportional to frequency.

items.stem: Jonas draws a histogram of the time taken to complete a puzzle. For the class 190 < t ≤ 290, which has frequency 40, Jonas draws a bar of height 40. Explain the error and give the correct height.
items.answer: The class width is 100, so the bar height must be the frequency density 40 ÷ 100 = 0.4.
items.markingKey: B1 must use frequency density; B1 0.4 [2]

items.stem: Mei draws a histogram of the length of phone calls. For the class 170 < t ≤ 270, which has frequency 500, Mei draws a bar of height 500. Explain the error and give the correct height.
items.answer: The class width is 100, so the bar height must be the frequency density 500 ÷ 100 = 5.

items.answer: 12 and 6

items.stem: A cumulative frequency curve
options: never decreases from left to right
has a maximum in the middle
items.answer: never decreases from left to right
items.markingKey: Running totals can only increase or stay the same.

items.stem: Answer both parts. (a) How is the interquartile range calculated? (b) Which measure of spread is not affected by extreme values?
items.answer: (a) Upper quartile − lower quartile (b) The interquartile range
items.markingKey: (a) IQR = Q₃ − Q₁, the range of the middle 50%. (b) It uses only the middle half of the data.
